subject: Feasibility ask: combined regulated-addenda pathing for K12 (FERPA) + bank (GLBA) pilot
messages:
From: Claire Harper <claire.harper@brightpath.edu>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot ask — FERPA + GLBA combined addendum feasibility

Marissa / Laura,

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. BrightPath Academy is planning a small pilot to power an educator-assist feature that will surface student records metadata (FERPA scope) and we have a parallel early pilot run with TrustBank for a loan-pre-qualification assistant (GLBA scope). Both teams are motivated to converge on a single deployment model to simplify integration and minimize latency, but their legal teams have different expectations around data residency, subprocessor disclosure (bank demands explicit residency in US-only for processing), and in BrightPath’s case the need for a FERPA-specific DPA clause and a signed BAA if any student health info surfaces.

High-level ask: can Redwood support a shared deployment approach (same service instance) while satisfying both sets of controls? Specifically:
- KMS options (customer-managed keys / HSM) and whether keys can be provisioned per-tenant
- Subprocessor residency commitments (US-only processing for TrustBank) and a current inventory export we can share with both counsel teams
- BAA scope and whether Redwood is comfortable adding a HIPAA/FERPA clause to a DPA for this pilot
- Audit logs / retention windows (TrustBank wants 7 years; BrightPath requests 3 years for student records)

We can share a redlined addendum from TrustBank counsel and a FERPA checklist from BrightPath. Would appreciate an initial feasibility note and any blockers before we loop counsel together.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min sync if useful.

Claire Harper
Dir, Product Operations — BrightPath Academy
claire.harper@brightpath.edu

Attachments: draft-trustbank-addendum.pdf (received from counsel), brightpath-ferpa-checklist.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Harper <claire.harper@brightpath.edu>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — FERPA + GLBA combined addendum feasibility

Claire — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the redlines. Looping in Laura (privacy/regulatory) and Marcus (infra/ops) to get an initial feasibility read.

Quick proposed approach from our side:
- We’ll produce a one-page feasibility memo that maps TrustBank and BrightPath asks to concrete controls (KMS, residency, logging, BAA scope).
- Deliverable: subprocessor inventory CSV + initial addendum outline (we can pre-populate requested clauses) within 24 business hours.
- For the short pilot, we’ll evaluate two deployment options: 1) Dedicated capacity with customer-managed KMS keys and enforced region controls, or 2) Private deployment (VPC) with shared control plane and on-prem KMS for strongest isolation.

Questions we’ll answer in the memo:
- Which clauses can be *committed* contractually vs which require operational mitigations (e.g., log retention differences enforced by per-tenant policies)
- Any blockers for a shared service instance spanning both customers (multi-tenant) vs recommending separate instances to avoid conflicting residency SLOs

I’ll circulate the memo and the inventory. Marcus — can you confirm whether we can export a per-tenant subprocessor residency assertion (CSV) and whether we can scope logging retention per customer today?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Claire Harper <claire.harper@brightpath.edu>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — FERPA + GLBA combined addendum feasibility

Marissa / Claire,

Summary (operational feasibility):
- KMS / Keys: We support customer-managed keys (CMK) via our KMS integration and can support HSM-backed keys through our KMS partners. Keys can be scoped per-customer; that will allow BrightPath and TrustBank to each provision their own keys. For a shared instance, we can still encrypt per-tenant artifacts with separate CMKs to meet isolation requirements.

- Residency / subprocessors: Our infra can guarantee processing in a single US region (we run dedicated pools in us-east-1 and us-west-2). We can produce a per-tenant subprocessor inventory export; I’ve attached the inventory CSV and an initial addendum outline for counsel to review. Note: some of our GPU runtime vendors have global support agreements — for those we mark as "region-agnostic" in the inventory, but we can provide contractual commitments to restrict placement to US-only hardware for the duration of the pilot via our Dedicated offering.

- BAA / HIPAA / FERPA: Redwood signs BAAs for customers that require them. Our standard DPA has an addendum template to cover HIPAA/FERPA language — we will not sign a BAA that extends to third-party SaaS features outside the agreed scope without an operational plan (e.g., what falls under PHI, what requires DB-level access). For BrightPath, if student health info is in-scope we recommend a Private deployment + CMK to keep keys under customer control; Dedicated with CMK is acceptable if BrightPath is comfortable with our Dedicated isolation model and the contractual stipulations.

- Audit logs / retention: We support configurable retention per tenant on our observability pipeline (minimum 30 days by default). We can extend to TrustBank’s 7-year requirement via an export + cold-storage workflow (S3 Glacier) — this is operationally supported but requires an addendum for storage costs and export SLA. BrightPath’s 3-year request is feasible via our managed retention settings with an agreed storage tier.

- Shared instance vs separate instances: Technically possible to run a shared service instance with per-tenant CMKs and per-tenant routing/policy enforcement. However, when customers have conflicting residency/retention SLOs (US-only vs lower retention), the safe recommendation for the pilot is to run separate Dedicated pools (or Private for BrightPath) to avoid entangling contractual guarantees. If both customers accept a documented operational mitigant (e.g., strict placement constraints + CMKs + documented retention exports), we can consider a shared Dedicated cluster for cost efficiency.

Attachments: redwood-subprocessor-inventory.csv; initial-addendum-outline.docx

I can be on a 30-min call this week to walk through the inventory and the respected clauses. If counsel wants, we can redact vendor-level commercial terms in the inventory but will provide residency + function-level mappings.

Marcus Lin
Head of Infrastructure & Ops — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
